resources.string: Andee needs this to see what is on screen and to tap, swipe and type for you. A floating ball appears on the home screen: tap it to talk, long-press to open the conversation.
These are deleted for good — there is no backup:
The device goes back to a fresh install: keys have to be entered again and the wake word has to be recorded again.
The conversation record and its pages are deleted, and everything said in this session is forgotten. The notebook is untouched.
Everything it noted down, your preferences, and any reminder not yet due are deleted, with no way back. The current chat history is untouched.
Takes effect when you close this panel — no need to restart the accessibility service.
Adds a Cloud backend tab for connecting to a hub you host yourself.

CodeFlying (CodeFlying.app) is connected: models and voice are set up and ready to go. You can also tap into a long list of third-party services — AI image, video and music generation, location, weather, PDF conversion, search, news, stocks and more. CodeFlying wraps and bills all of them in one place, so you never have to sign up with each provider or juggle their keys and invoices.

Account and top-ups: open CodeFlying.app in a computer browser and sign in. If you see a balance error (HTTP 402), top up there.

Note: using CodeFlying backend services may incur charges.

Want Andee to draw, make videos, write music, check the weather, search the news, convert PDFs, or watch stocks for you? Connect CodeFlying: models and voice come set up, and a long list of third-party services is one hookup away, with no separate sign-ups, keys or invoices.

To get started, open CodeFlying.app in a computer browser and generate your own Andee install package in one click, then install it over this app. New users get free credit, so you can try it first.

Note: using CodeFlying backend services may incur charges.
What the hub should call this device
The brain lives on a hub you run yourself; this device only acts.
The device runs the agent loop itself, with no hub. Without a key it will not take over.
Enrolled — say your wake word while the screen is on
Not enrolled — pick a phrase and say it 3 times to wake me by voice, e.g. “Hey Andee”
No accounts yet — once saved, Andee can log in as you when a task needs it
%1$d saved — the brain may read the phone and email, but only this device types the password
The source ships without a key. Enter your own to hear and speak; leave the rows below blank for the default endpoints.
Volcengine Speech key — hearing and speaking both need it
nothing yet — hearing and speaking are off
The most tool calls the AI may make in a single task before stopping with a final answer. Guards against runaway loops and bills. Default 25 — a dozen steps is enough for most tasks.
Show the cloud option, typing, diagnostics and factory reset. Nothing here for day-to-day use.
Records coordinate taps and screenshots to files/grounding for offline analysis — it photographs whatever you are doing. Needs the accessibility service restarted to take effect.

Once a conversation goes quiet it reviews it by itself: keeps what is worth keeping, schedules what it owes. On by default — this is where \\"it remembers\\" comes from. Off means it stops spending your key on those calls.

When a message arrives it decides for itself whether it is worth your attention: lets the noise go, says the useful part out loud, handles what needs handling. \"Chat apps\" means the ones with a person on the other end — WeChat, QQ, DingTalk, Lark, SMS. \"Everything\" watches the rest too, minus progress bars and permanent notifications. It only puts a card up when it cannot decide. Off means nothing interrupts you — the messages are all still there, and you can ask about them whenever.
ADBKeyboard is the only keyboard on this device and it has no keyboard UI, so nothing can be typed right now. Enable one in system settings and it will show up here.

Normally it is your own keyboard, and you can type in any app. While I am typing something for you it switches to ADBKeyboard (which has no keyboard UI — that is the only way it works), and switches straight back.
Pages it has built for you
Nothing here yet.\nAsk it to build you a page — say, “make me a pomodoro timer”.
How should “%1$s” change? Say it or type it
Ways of working it worked out with you
No scenes yet.\nDo the same kind of thing with it a few times — English practice, say — and it will offer to save it as a scene. Or just say “save this as a scene”.
To change a scene, just tell it — e.g. “in English practice, only correct one mistake at a time”
Nothing is saved until you tap Adopt. After that it is yours like any other scene: change it or delete it whenever you like.
(This app was hiding its screen; turned on the system\'s accessibility enhance service so it shows it again)
the Volcano and DeepSeek keys, and every speech and brain setting
the notebook: what it remembers and what it promised
the accounts, passwords and bank cards kept in the vault
the wake-word recordings (they will have to be recorded again)
the conversation history and the pages it generated
cookies and local storage left behind by the pages it drew
Accounts saved here let Andee log in for you when a task needs it.\nIt types the password into the field itself and never hands it to the remote brain.
Feishu / work email — the brain finds it by this name
The password is only typed into the field, never returned to the brain.
Hints like “sign in with an SMS code” — the brain can read these

The number, expiry and CVV work like the password: typed into the field, never returned to the brain. Payment sheets in Alipay / WeChat / a banking app draw their own keypad and cannot be typed into — what this reaches is an ordinary checkout form or a card-binding page. Paying is still yours to confirm.
The name printed on the card — the brain can read this

Pick any word or phrase you like to call me by, for example “Hey Andee”. Aim for something that takes at least half a second to say — very short words are easy to confuse and may not record at all. Tap Start, then say it the way you normally would — it stops on its own. You\'ll say the same thing %1$d times — don\'t say it more carefully than usual, or I won\'t recognise it when you call me normally.
Already recorded — recording again will overwrite it.
Not recorded yet. Think of a phrase (e.g. “Hey Andee”), then tap Start.
Didn\'t catch that — move closer, then wait half a second after you finish before checking the screen.
Done — just say your wake word while the screen is on. (threshold %1$s)
Point at a QR code / barcode
Notification access (know when you get messages)
A dialog will pop up — just tap Allow.
I\'ll open Notification access settings — find this app and turn it on.
Send as is, or add a few words…
I\'m on a call — tell me once it\'s hung up.
The only keyboard on this device is ADBKeyboard, and it has no UI — nothing can be typed.\nTurn on an input method in system settings and it will work.
(Meeting recording ended — %1$d characters, drafting the minutes…)
(%1$s has a message — I tapped "Take a look"…)
(%1$s has a message — taking a look myself…)
No brain is connected yet, so I can\'t speak.
The local brain has no key yet, so I can\'t speak.
"(Listed by type and most-recently updated; read-only)\n\n"
When the time comes but I can\'t wake up, at least say it clearly
%1$s\n\n(When the time came I wasn\'t running, so I couldn\'t do it for you. Turn on the accessibility service and I\'ll pick it back up.)
Recording %1$d:%2$02d · tap the ball to stop
The on-device brain has no API key yet — long-press the ball, open settings and put a DeepSeek key in the Brain section.
The backend answered 402, which most likely means the account is out of balance. Open Settings → Backend to see which provider you are using, then top up on that provider\'s website and try again.
The backend answered 402, which most likely means your CodeFlying balance has run out. Open CodeFlying.app in a computer browser, sign in, top up, and try again.
The backend refused the request (HTTP %1$d): the key is wrong, expired or disabled. Check the key in Settings → Backend, and generate a new one on the provider\'s website if needed.
The backend rejected the request: %1$s\nThe usual cause is a misspelled model name. Check it in Settings → Backend.
The backend could not find that address (HTTP 404). Check the endpoint URL and the model name in Settings → Backend.
The backend is busy or being asked too often (HTTP 429). Say it again in a moment. If it keeps happening, check on the provider\'s website whether your quota has run out.
The backend itself is having trouble (HTTP %1$d). Your settings are not the problem. Try again in a few minutes, or check the provider\'s website for maintenance notices.
The backend took too long to answer. Check that the network is working and try again in a moment.
I could not reach the backend. Check this device\'s network; if that is fine, check the endpoint URL in Settings → Backend.
I got nothing back that time — say it again.
I kept doing the same thing over and over (%1$s), so I stopped — that way is blocked. Try saying it differently, or take over.
I have spent %1$d steps on this without finishing, so I stopped to ask: shall I try another way, or will you take over?
On. The ball and every screen action are running.

Off. No ball, no voice, no tapping or swiping — with this one off, the rest of this list does not matter yet. The switch lives under "Downloaded apps" in the accessibility settings, not on the first screen.
Allowed. The ball can be drawn.
Off. Neither the ball nor any card can be drawn, while the service runs perfectly well in the background — which is why it looks like nothing happened at all.
Offline. Speech recognition, speech synthesis and every model call go over the network.

Not set. The brain is set to the cloud, so the address of your own hub goes in ⚙ → “Brain” → “Hub URL”. Without it there is nowhere to send what you say: no answers, and nothing on screen moves. To have this device think for itself, switch the brain to “On-device” in the same place.

Not set. The brain is set to run on this device, so open a DeepSeek account of your own and put the key in ⚙ → “Brain” → “DeepSeek Key”. Without it, what you say arrives and nothing can be answered or acted on.
Cloud assistant — the model is not on this device.
No key yet. Fill one in and this becomes testable.
Reachable but rate-limited (HTTP 429). The configuration is right; it recovers on its own.
The server answered %1$s: most likely the account is out of balance. Top up on the current provider\'s website and try again.
No model called “%1$s” on this server. It offers: %2$s
%1$s is available; you are on %2$s. The old one still works — update whenever you like.
Update to %1$s. The build you are on (%2$s) is no longer supported.
Offline, so not tested. You are on %1$s.
Today\'s checks are used up; they reset tomorrow. You are on %1$s.
Could not be checked: %1$s. You are on %2$s.
Granted, and the listener is bound.
Settings says “granted”, but the listener is not bound — notifications are being dropped silently.\nThis one only comes back if you turn it off and then on again; leaving it on does nothing.
Off. Call announcements and forwarded notifications never arrive.
Through the accessibility input method: I can type into a field myself — no keyboard to install, no default input method to change, no computer to plug in. Your own keyboard stays active throughout.
This Android version (below 13) has no accessibility input method, so typing goes through the ADB keyboard below — both of those rows have to be in place.
Enabled. It can type into other apps for you.
Not needed now — typing goes through the accessibility input method. It stays as the spare: a field that channel cannot reach falls back to this one, and it has to be installed by then.
Installed but not enabled. Turn it on in system settings — it has no keyboard UI of its own, so enabling it does not get in the way of typing yourself.
Not installed. Typing and filling in forms for you go through it (ADBKeyboard), so that does not work yet. Download it with the button here — when you come back this row is a one-tap enable.
Granted. Typing into other apps works.
Not granted, so typing into other apps (type_text) is unavailable. There is no switch for this in Settings — it can only be given over adb with the cable plugged in.
Not granted, and typing works anyway — it goes through the accessibility input method. This is only needed by the spare channel above.
Not allowed. Tapping the ball does nothing at all — the failure that least resembles a permission problem.
Set. Recognition and synthesis use it to reach Volcengine.

Not set. The source ships without a key — open a Volcengine Speech service of your own and put the key in ⚙ → “Speech (Volcengine)” → “Volcengine API key”. Without it, hearing and speaking cannot connect, and what you get back is a connection timeout that looks like a network fault. Everything else works.
Could not reach %1$s: %2$s. Both recognition and synthesis will time out.
Taught, and it wakes while the screen is on.
Not taught yet. Pick a phrase (e.g. “Hey Andee”) and say it 3 times to wake me by voice. Everything still works without it, you just tap the ball to talk.
Exempt, so pending reminders are not delayed.

Not exempt from battery optimisation. Tap “Open settings” — the system asks “Ignore battery optimisations?”; take the button that ignores them.\nThe vendor’s own “App launch / background running” controls are a separate system; changing them leaves this row red. With the screen off a pending reminder may arrive late, and the wake phrase stops listening.
Only %1$d MB left; screenshots and pages will start going missing.
Only %1$d MB left — almost nothing can be written.
This one can only be done from a computer, over adb:
This device has no such settings screen. You will have to find it in Settings yourself.
Where this device stands right now.
Everything is set up. Tap the ball and talk.
The rest is just for reference and changes nothing.
The settings sheet is drawn as a floating window — turn on “Draw over other apps” below first, then come back and fill these in.
A few steps to get this device ready. Each one asks you to grant a permission or fill a setting. Tap Next when you\'re done.
Pick a phrase and say it 3 times (e.g. “Hey Andee”) — you can then call me by voice when the screen is on. Works without one too; you\'d just tap the ball instead.
Let it see where you are now so it remembers this place. Later when you ask "where am I" it can answer.
Tap the ball, say something — it\'ll answer, and setup is done.
Go tap the ball and talk. Long-press it to unfold the card, ⚙ opens settings.
